discharge_profile.primary_diagnosis: Severe Right Lower Lobe Community-Acquired Pneumonia, resolved sepsis
procedures: Inpatient IV Ceftriaxone and Azithromycin therapy, transitioned to oral antibiotics
discharge_profile.dietary_instructions: Well-balanced diet, generous oral hydration (at least 2 Liters of water daily to thin pulmonary secretions).
discharge_profile.activity_restrictions: Gradual return to activities. Daily rest periods. Avoid tobacco smoke and environmental irritants.
discharge_profile.wound_care_instructions: No surgical wounds. Monitor IV catheter puncture sites for phlebitis.

medications.frequency: Once daily for 5 more days (Finish full course!)
medications.indication: Targeted oral antibiotic to eradicate residual pulmonary infection
medications.warning: CRITICAL: Complete the full course even if feeling better. Report tendon pain.

medications.frequency: 1-2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or tightness
Every 12 hours with full glass of water

red_flag_warnings: Oxygen saturation (SpO2) dropping to 90% or lower on pulse oximeter
Return of high fever (101.5°F / 38.6°C or higher) or severe rigors/shaking chills
Coughing up significant amounts of bright red blood (hemoptysis)
Sharp pleuritic chest pain that worsens when breathing deeply

initial_care_tasks_day_2.title: Morning Antibiotic (Levofloxacin 750mg)
initial_care_tasks_day_2.description: Take 1 tablet with a full glass of water. Must be completed daily without skipping.

initial_care_tasks_day_2.title: Resting Pulse Oximeter & Temp Check
initial_care_tasks_day_2.description: Measure SpO2 and body temperature. Oxygen should remain above 92%.

initial_care_tasks_day_2.title: Midday Respiratory Symptom Check-in
initial_care_tasks_day_2.description: Check in regarding cough, sputum color, and ease of breathing.
